sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Montgomery County, Tennessee?
sections.html:
Two county offices share the work, and they sit next to each other in Veterans Plaza at 350 Pageant Lane in Clarksville. The Assessor of Property, Suite 101-C, values the land and buildings; the County Trustee, Suite 101-B, sends and collects the bills.

  • Assessor of Property: Erinne Hester, phone 931-648-5709, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • County Trustee: 931-648-5717, open weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Delinquent suits: Clerk and Master, Montgomery Chancery Court, 2 Millennium Plaza, Suite 101, 931-648-5703.

The Board of Commissioners sets the county rate. The Trustee then applies it to each $100 of assessed value. For a house inside Clarksville city limits, the City of Clarksville sends a second bill, so a seller there has two balances to clear.

sections.h2: What does Montgomery County look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Montgomery County dates to 1796, and Clarksville is both the county seat and its only incorporated municipality. The county sits in the Clarksville, TN-KY metropolitan area. Census QuickFacts puts the July 2025 population at 249,935, a 13.6% rise over the 2020 base of 220,012.

Housing and income figures from the same Census table show a county that is mostly owner-occupied and fast growing.

  • Housing units, July 2025: 102,547.
  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 2024: 61.9%.
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $280,200.
  • Median household income: $75,613.
  • Median gross rent: $1,308.
  • Veterans living in the county: 30,166.

The county covers 539 square miles of land with about 408 people per square mile. Mean commute is 27.8 minutes. A house valued at the median figure and billed at the residential 25% ratio would have an assessed value of $70,050, which makes the arithmetic of a tax bill easy to check.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 tax rates and how is a Montgomery County bill calculated?
sections.html:
The Trustee's FAQ gives the 2026 county rate as $2.10 per $100 of assessed value, and Clarksville's FAQ lists the city rate as $1.01. A property inside the city therefore carries a combined $3.11 per $100.

Assessed value is a share of appraised value that depends on use: residential and farm are 25%, commercial and industrial 40%, personal property 30%, and public utilities 55%. The Trustee's method is to multiply the appraisal by the class percentage, divide by 100, then multiply by the rate.

Sample 2026 bill on a $280,200 home in Montgomery County
StepOutside ClarksvilleInside Clarksville
Assessed value at 25%$70,050$70,050
County tax at $2.10 per $100$1,471.05$1,471.05
City tax at $1.01 per $100None$707.51
Total$1,471.05$2,178.56

Source: Montgomery County Trustee FAQ and City of Clarksville FAQ. The home value is the Census median, used only as an illustration, so your own bill will differ. Compare the figures against the notice you receive.

sections.h2: When are Montgomery County property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Statements go out in the last week of October. Payment opens on the first Monday of October and stays interest-free through the last day of February. From March 1, the county adds 1.5 percent a month, which is 18 percent over a year.

Tennessee does not require the Trustee to mail a notice, and the county says a missing bill does not excuse a late payment. Partial payments on the current year are allowed from July 10, provided the balance is cleared by the February deadline. Mailed payments count as paid on the postmark date, but the office does not accept its own meter dates.

Online, an e-check costs 1.75 percent plus $1, and Visa or MasterCard costs 2.65 percent plus $1. Cash is accepted only in person. Local banks also take current-year payments from October through February 28 if you carry the original bill or a printout from the Trustee's website.

Clarksville is stricter about the aftermath. Its FAQ says the city hands taxes to its delinquent tax attorney once they are a full year late, and later payments go to the Clerk and Master at the chancery court.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Montgomery County assessment?
sections.html:
Call the Assessor first at 931-648-5709. A short conversation often clears up a wrong square footage or classification. If that does not settle it, the next stop is the County Board of Equalization, which convenes on the first business day of June and keeps sitting until the year's work is done.

Hearing appointments open by phone after May 15 and before June 1. The board has five property owners from different parts of the county, and Tennessee law requires two of them to be Clarksville residents. You may attend yourself or send a family member, an attorney or an authorized agent. Bring appraisals, repair receipts and comparable assessments, and leave out arguments about whether you can afford the tax, because the board only weighs value.

Decisions are usually mailed before the end of June. A further appeal goes to the State Board of Equalization, due by August 1 or 45 days after the county letter is mailed, whichever is later. Montgomery County's next countywide reappraisal is scheduled for 2029, according to the Assessor.

sections.h2: What tax relief and special bills affect a Montgomery County sale?
sections.html:
Tennessee reimburses part of the tax for low-income elderly and disabled homeowners and for disabled veterans and surviving spouses. The Comptroller's tax relief page says this is repayment, not an exemption, so the bill still arrives and must be paid. Relief covers one primary residence, and a trust-owned house does not qualify.

In Clarksville, the Trustee's office is where you sign up for the Tax Freeze program, and relief applications are available at both the county Trustee and the city Finance and Revenue Department. Approved owners get a voucher with each bill and must send it in every year to both offices.

Greenbelt land brings another charge. If a sale ends the farm, forest or open-space classification, rollback taxes for the previous three years (five for open space) come due, and unless the contract says otherwise the seller owes them. A buyer who promises to keep the classification has 90 days after the sale to file the form with the Assessor, or the rollback becomes the buyer's problem. Unpaid rollback tax is a first lien on the land either way.

sections.h2: How is Montgomery County property tax handled at closing?
sections.html:
The Trustee's FAQ tells new owners to read the closing statement or ask the title company who pays the year's tax. Unpaid tax stays attached to the property no matter who agreed to pay it. Clarksville's FAQ adds a warning: a property with delinquent taxes can still be sold at a tax auction, whatever the sale contract says.

Before closing, ask the Trustee for the county balance and the city Finance and Revenue office for the city balance. Check whether your mortgage servicer already paid from escrow, because the city refunds a double payment to whoever paid last. Then ask the title company to pay any balance still owed out of the seller's proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the Montgomery County property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The county rate is $2.10 per $100 of assessed value, and Clarksville adds $1.01 for homes inside the city. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value.

faqs.q: When must Montgomery County property tax be paid?
faqs.a: Pay between the first Monday of October and the last day of February to avoid interest. Starting March 1, interest of 1.5 percent a month is added to the base tax.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Montgomery County assessment?
faqs.a: Start with the Assessor at 931-648-5709, then book a hearing with the County Board of Equalization by phone between May 15 and June 1. A further appeal to the State Board of Equalization is due by August 1 or 45 days after the county letter.

faqs.q: Do I owe city tax and county tax on a Clarksville house?
faqs.a: Yes. A house inside Clarksville pays both, and the Trustee collects only the county portion. Outside city limits you pay county tax only.

faqs.q: Who pays Montgomery County property tax when a house sells?
faqs.a: The sale contract and closing statement decide it. Tennessee taxes cover the calendar year and stay attached to the property, so ask the title company to confirm the split and to pay any balance from the seller's proceeds.
